macro.regime: Hawkish-Fed war-shock: equities still pricing complacency
macro.narrative: The regime holds unchanged from Friday, with two fresh data points reinforcing rather than resolving it. First, equities rallied into the weekly close (S&P +0.51% to 7,743.41, Dow snapping a 3-week losing streak) even as the 10-year Treasury yield pushed to 5.18% -- its highest since the 2008 financial crisis -- a genuine divergence between calm equity positioning and stressed rates markets that BlackRock's Rick Rieder called 'not a crisis but an eye-opener.' Second, the BofA Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep) showed fund flows reversing sharply: US equity funds lost $21.1bn versus +$63.8bn the prior week, suggesting institutional positioning is starting to react to the hawkish Fed even as the cash index rallied -- a divergence worth watching rather than a reason to shift stance yet. On the geopolitical leg, Iran issued a 4-5 day ultimatum on Hormuz reopening (expiring ~Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep) after Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub, while Brent eased on truce-hope headlines to ~$105.3 -- still a live, two-sided catalyst with a hard near-term deadline. Gold and silver extended their pullback into Friday on the firmer dollar/higher-real-yield backdrop -- a macro-driven move, not a reversal of the structural bull case (record central-bank buying, a 5th consecutive annual silver supply deficit). This week's Trump-Xi Washington summit held the trade truce at status quo with no new concessions on rare-earth magnet flows (Aug US-bound shipments still -21% MoM), reinforcing rather than resolving the China rare-earth leverage theme. Credit spreads remain historically tight, leaving little cushion if the Iran deadline is missed or the Fed's hiking cycle bites growth harder than currently priced.
